courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Introduction to Industrial Design
courses.description: Introduction to problem-finding and problem-solving processes in the design of products. This course teaches foundational industrial design skills, methods, philosophies, and design thinking. Creation of 3-dimensional products begins with a simplified design process, adding steps until a final project is completed that incorporates all components of the design process. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to Art and Design majors.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Introduction to Graphic Design
courses.description: Provides a foundational exploration of visual perception, communication theory, and graphic design history, while developing technical proficiencies in typography, layout, image‑making, and digital mock‑ups. Students engage in studio projects that treat graphic design as a critical‑thinking and problem‑solving process. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to Art and Design majors.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Industrial Design I
courses.description: Introduction to the creative process and methods involved in industrial design; research, modeling, form giving, prototyping and communication with emphasis on user centered design. Projects of escalating scale and complexity complemented by lectures and demonstrations. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Completion of the First-Year Curriculum in Art & Design. Concurrent registration in ARTD 225.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Industrial Design II
courses.description: Studio design problems of increasing complexity involving structures and mechanisms. Lectures and discussions to explore design issues affecting contemporary culture and aesthetics perceptions. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 201. Concurrent registration in ARTD 228.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Introduction to Image Making
courses.description: This introductory studio functions as a survey of representational strategies through image reproduction technology. Discussions center around the reader's construction of meaning through still and moving images. Students develop an authorial voice in visual practice. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Sophomore standing in graphic design curriculum or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Graphic Design for Non-Majors
courses.description: ARTS EXCHANGE: Introduces students to the field of graphic design in theory and practice. Examines what graphic designers make and the methods that are employed in contemporary design practice. Emphasis is placed on the organization and visual presentation of relevant content across media and their effect within systems. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to students in FAA or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Interaction Design Foundation
courses.description: Builds foundational fluency in interaction design — screen layout, information architecture, and design systems alongside hands-on development in current industry standard coding languages. In this studio course, students design and implement interactions triggered by analog inputs, grounded in user-centered thinking and accessibility standards.
courses.prereqText: Completion of the First-Year Curriculum in Art & Design.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Typography 1
courses.description: Introduces the foundations of typographic form, composition, and meaning through the study of letterforms, structure, and spatial organization. Students explore the relationship between type and communication while developing technical fluency in typesetting, composition, and layout. Emphasis is placed on visual hierarchy, typographic systems, and the integration of type and image as vehicles for clarity and expression. Develops proficiency in industry-standard typographic software. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Completion of the First-Year Curriculum in Art & Design.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Design Drawing
courses.description: Introduction to rapid drawing methods and tools used by designers. Focuses on theory and application of orthographic and perspective drawing for communication of design ideas. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Industrial Design majors must have completed the First-Year Curriculum in Art & Design. Industrial Design majors must have concurrent registration in ARTD 201. Sustainable Design majors are restricted by sophomore standing.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Computer Applications
courses.description: Concepts, methods and applications of computer-aided industrial design to the design of products for mass manufacture. Rendering and lighting techniques to communicate product forms. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Concurrent registration in ARTD 202.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Design Thinking/Need-Finding
courses.description: Design thinking, a term with origins in industrial design practice, describes a human-centered approach to design and innovation in products and services, addressing the tri-partite requirements of feasibility, desirability and viability. With this focus on determining user needs, a variety of processes, including observation, empathy, ideation, prototyping and modeling, are used to discover people's needs and opportunities for design thinking, along with the communication of design outcomes by diagrammatic and narrative means. Design thinking is best done in teams, hence the project team basis for this course. This course concentrates on need-finding rather than the full resolution of design proposals. Same as TE 230. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: For Art+Design or Engineering majors only.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: eWaste: Sustainable Design
courses.description: Examines the topics of electronic waste, or eWaste, within the context of sustainable design. Students will learn about sustainable and "green" electronic product design practices and develop the ability to assess a variety of products according to these criteria. Case studies will be supplemented by assigned readings, directed writing, and group discussion.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Graphic Design Toolbox
courses.description: This studio introduces students to the field of graphic design in theory and practice. The course examines what graphic designers make and the methods that are employed in contemporary design practice. Emphasis is placed on the organization and visual presentation of relevant content across media and their effect within systems. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Completion of the First-Year Curriculum in Art & Design.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Design Methods
courses.description: Design Methods is a hybrid studio and seminar that introduces students to the principles and process of human-centered design through a focus on research and observation outside of the studio. This approach will allow students to address the social and cultural contexts in which designers intervene. Through a series of exercises and projects, students will begin to develop competencies in conducting research in specific environments in order to inform and inspire the direction of their design projects. Students will also learn how to iterate design solutions and prototypes based on expert input, testing and user feedback. Students will better understand and articulate the tools and methodologies shared by all design disciplines as it relates to a variety of actions and outcomes: visual communication and the design of objects, services, interactions and experiences. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Graphic Design majors must have completed the First-Year Curriculum in Art & Design. Sustainable Design majors are restricted by sophomore standing.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Creative Coding
courses.description: Focuses on the foundational concepts and skills of programming through simple design challenges, including bitmap manipulation and gesture-based interactions. Learn to code interactive digital canvases for desktop and mobile devices. Develop the ability to program a computer to create solutions to simple visual and interactive design problems. With the skills acquired over the development of this class, students will discover code as a form of creative expression using diverse media.
courses.prereqText: CS 124 or similar course in computer programming. Restricted to Graphic Design or Industrial Design major(s) or Art and Design minor(s). Not intended for students with Freshman class standing.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Computational Design 1
courses.description: Studio which explores the design of interactive solutions using computational thinking to address design challenges. Students leverage their interests and imagination to explore the language and aesthetics of digital media to prototype creative solutions, including experimental user-interface design and non-linear visual narratives. Emphasizing human-centered design principles, the curriculum guides students through user observation, problem formulation, conceptual framing, and proof-of-concept prototyping.
courses.prereqText: CS 124. ARTD 151 OR ARTD 101. Restricted to Graphic Design or Industrial Design major(s) or Art and Design minor(s). Not intended for students with Freshman class standing.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Spec Topics in Design Courses
courses.description: Topics and subject matter to be published in course listings. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 12 hours but no more than 6 hours in any one term.
courses.prereqText: Sophomore standing in Art and Design.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Industrial Design III
courses.description: Design of user centered products for mass production; experience in the iterative problem solving processes and methods. Addresses practical constraints such as sustainability, environmental factors/ergonomics, manufacturing and materials, social and political and economic. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 202.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Industrial Design IV
courses.description: Industrial design problems of increasing complexity, scope and size. Continuation of ARTD 301. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 301.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: UI/UX Design for Non-Majors
courses.description: This User interface/User experience (UI/UX) studio introduces the non-designer to the construction of compelling user experiences that incorporate the use of digital products/code. Students investigate both the theoretical and practical aspects of UI/UX through projects involving information architecture, user scenarios, wireframing, interface design, and creative code for web and mobile products. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Interaction Design
courses.description: This studio explores the construction of compelling user experiences that incorporate the use of digital media. Students investigate both the theoretical and practical aspects of interaction through exercises involving information architecture, interface design, and creative code. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 218.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Sustainability & Manufacturing
courses.description: Exploration of environmental origins, theory and practice of sustainable product design. Environmentally-responsive design methodologies and topics such as industrial ecology, dematerialization, design for disassembly, design for recycling and life-cycle assessment. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing in Art and Design or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Human-Centered Product Design
courses.description: Principles of human-centered design and usability applied to products, product systems, and product environments to enhance the user experience; strategies to enhance independent learning for professional development, to further research, and to acquire new skills. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to Junior standing in Art and Design or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Typography 2
courses.description: Builds on foundational typographic principles through advanced exploration of type and image relationships. This studio course introduces applied design projects that extend typographic thinking across varied contexts, emphasizing the development of complex typographic systems and structures. Students investigate how type interacts with images, materials, and formats to convey meaning, coherence, and expression across multi-page and multi-platform compositions. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 222.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Graphic Design Inquiry
courses.description: A series of topical studios that touch upon the myriad practices of graphic design. Students produce and analyze form and content according to each individual topic. Media engagement varies across sections. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. May be repeated up to 8 hours.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Graphic Design Practicum
courses.description: This analytical studio prepares students for entry into the field of graphic design. Professional practice is parsed into areas of opportunity, to which students ultimately align themselves and by which they structure their preparatory endeavors. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Credit in ARTD 333, credit or concurrent registration in ARTD 318, and senior standing.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Computational Design 2
courses.description: Explore the potential of computers to act as co-creators or independent creators by assisting designers with these cycles or conducting them autonomously. Engage with the design process as a series of creative iterations of analysis and synthesis, during which data is sorted, clustered, summarized, and generated.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 282. Restricted to Graphic Design or Industrial Design major(s) or Art and Design minor(s). Not intended for students with Freshman class standing.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Special Problems in Design
courses.description: Directed independent creative activity or research. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 6 hours.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing in Art and Design; and consent of instructor, advisor, and associate director of the School. A contract must be completed & approved by the instructor & advisor. 3.3 GPA, & only 6 hours total Ind. Study.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Internship in Design
courses.description: Internships to be pre-approved for variable credit. Students will be required to document work completed during the internship with verification of supervisor. Supervisor will also be required to fill out a questionnaire either by mail or on-line. Faculty members will assess work and questionnaires to assign a grade. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in the same term up to 4 UG hours or in separate terms up to 4 UG hours.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to Junior standing in School of Art and Design. Registration only with instructor permission, complete the Undergraduate Internship Study form at art.illinois.edu.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Industrial Design V
courses.description: Advanced design projects in the context of the business environment in which product design and development takes place; marketing, branding, merchandizing, entrepreneurship within the context of globalized marketing and manufacturing. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. 4 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 302.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Industrial Design VI
courses.description: Capstone project integrating all aspects of the design process from concept through final design, documentation and presentation; reconciliation of user centered constraints such as socio-economic, environmental-sustainability, manufacturability, health and safety and ethical. Standard approach that of an entry level industrial design professional. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. 4 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 401.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Advanced Interaction Design
courses.description: This advanced studio immerses students in design investigations that foster understanding of emergent digital interaction paradigms. Potential areas of exploration include design and development for both mobile devices and interactive environments. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 318.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Disability Design
courses.description: Focuses on user-oriented, collaborative approaches to designing new products and services, with special emphasis on designing for people with disabilities. Students gain an understanding of the product development process by exploring empathic design research approaches, while working directly with prospective clients. Course work centers on designing products for mass production, and on recognizing opportunities to re-engineer existing products. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Product Innovation
courses.description: Presents an overview of the product development process from concept generation to design for manufacturing and project management. Emphasis on product definition, innovation, the early phases of development and the role of designer in new product development. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Typography 3
courses.description: Advances typographic research, experimentation, and creative practice through systemic and narrative design. The course emphasizes typographic authorship, material exploration, and the integration of type, image, and content across print, digital, and environmental contexts. Students investigate how typography shapes meaning, narrative, and aesthetic expression while developing a personal typographic voice. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 333.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Seminar in Responsible Design
courses.description: Investigation of special problems and current topics in industrial and/or graphic design. Students will conduct original research which will be shared through papers, presentations, and discussions. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 12 undergraduate hours or 16 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to Juniors in Art and Design or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Professional Design Practice
courses.description: Concentrates on developing presentation and communication skills that form the basis of a successful design career. Students will engage in portfolio reviews, plan and install exhibitions, prepare client presentations, and rehearse job interviews. Written work will include CV preparation. Emphasis will be placed on familiarizing students with professional practices and contexts. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Ethics of a Designer in a Global Economy
courses.description: Ethics of a Designer in a Global Economy (EDGE) studio presents complex problems of ethics within the graphic design practice. Individual sections address social and environmental issues. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. 4 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated up to 8 hours in the same term and 12 hours in separate terms, if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: Sustainable Design majors are restricted by junior standing.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Interaction Design Problems
courses.description: This series of topical studios presents complex problems of user experience through interactive media. Individual sections address professional, theoretical, or exploratory problems. Technological engagement varies across sections. 1 to 4 undergraduate hours. 1 to 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 222 and ARTD 318.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Graphic Design Capstone
courses.description: Students in this advanced studio articulate individual interests and conduct corresponding investigations to develop specialized expertise. The coursework represents the student's final preparation for practice in graphic design. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 371.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Advanced Design Inquiry
courses.description: Explores the integration of graphic, interaction, and industrial design through projects informed by the instructor’s research. Individual sections emphasize different aspects of design: theoretical approaches, human-centered and other-than-human-centered design, conceptual synthesis, prototyping methods, material and digital experimentation, and cohesive communication across multiple systems of impact. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated in separate terms up to 6 undergraduate hours or up to 8 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to senior standing and graduate students. Restricted to Graphic Design, Industrial Design, Master of Design, and Master of Fine Arts in Art and Design, concentrations in Industrial Design or Design for Responsible Innovation.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Computational Design 3
courses.description: Capstone studio which requires students to integrate the technical skills and critical theoretical frameworks acquired in the previous computational design studios. Define and carry out a significant independent project to showcase mastery of algorithmic thinking, data-driven workflows, and creating novel digital or physical artifacts. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 382 and one elective in Human-Centered Design ( ARTD 328, ARTD 270, ART 310 or other approved with consent of instructor). Restricted to Graphic Design or Industrial Design major(s) or Art and Design minor(s). Not intended for students with Freshman class standing.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Computational Design Seminar
courses.description: Explores how computational tools and processes are redefining what it means to design today. Examine the "how" and "why" behind the tools used in design, reflect on the intellectual property issues and ethical responsibilities that come with them. By studying creative work and real-world cultural contexts, students gain a deeper understanding of how machine learning and artificial intelligence are reshaping the design discipline. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 282 or consent of instructor. Restricted to Graphic Design, or Industrial Design major(s), or Art and Design minor(s), or Art and Design Graduate Students. Not intended for students with Freshman class standing.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Advanced Prototyping for Industrial Design
courses.description: Explores advanced prototyping techniques and processes for design inquiry and validation. Students engage in iterative workflows combining sketching, physical and digital modeling, fabrication, and visualization. Key topics include reverse engineering real products using SolidWorks, preparing files for 3D printing, advanced finishing techniques, and hybrid assembly. Visualization skills are developed through KeyShot rendering and photo shoots, enabling students to create high-quality models and portfolio-ready documentation. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to undergraduate juniors, seniors, or graduate standing students.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Visual Communication for Industrial Design
courses.description: Equips students with essential visual communication skills for the field of industrial design. Focusing on sketching, composition, layout, and storytelling, the course treats visual communication as both a tool for thinking and a persuasive medium. Students learn to create, document, and present professional design work with clarity and intent, culminating in a process book and portfolio suitable for advanced academic and professional contexts. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to undergraduate juniors, seniors, or graduate standing students.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Human-Centered Design Research
courses.description: Introduces advanced undergraduate and graduate students to essential design research methods, blending qualitative and quantitative approaches within human-centered design frameworks. Students learn to frame complex problems, conduct primary and secondary research, synthesize data, and translate findings into actionable design opportunities. Emphasizing ethics, reflexivity, and cultural awareness, the course prepares students to create impactful research portfolios for advanced studio work, thesis research, and professional design practice. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to Senior, Graduate standing or consent of instructor required.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Special Topics in Design
courses.description: Topics and subject matter to be published in course listings. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. 1 to 3 undergraduate hours. 1 to 4 graduate hours. May be repeated if topics vary to a maximum of 9 undergraduate or 12 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Senior standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Industrial Design I: From Inquiry to Ideation
courses.description: After a quick benchmarking exercise to determine students' current level of design skills, this course focuses on the first stages of design thinking using research and analysis to determine user needs and going on to ideation and creative thinking strategies to respond to those needs. This course is the first in a sequence leading to a MFA in Industrial Design, MDes in Industrial Design, or Advanced Design Thinking Graduate Certificate. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: BFA in Industrial Design or a related field (as accepted by the faculty), or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Industrial Design II: From Ideation to Implementation
courses.description: Builds on the research and insights carried out in ARTD 501 to generate ideas and concepts that answer the identified needs, and to develop those into resolved design proposals. This course is the second in a sequence leading to a MFA in Industrial Design, MDes in Industrial Design, or Advanced Design Thinking Graduate Certificate. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 501.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Industrial Design III: Design Project Formulation
courses.description: Emphasizes all aspects of the research and design process in a holistic design project intended as a rehearsal for the thesis investigations and establishing a personal direction for students' work. This course is the third in a sequence leading to a MFA in Industrial Design or MDes in Industrial Design. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 502.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Industrial Design IV: Thesis Research
courses.description: Research activities of the master's thesis design project, individually negotiated and supervised by a thesis committee. This is the first course in the ID master's thesis project sequence for the MFA and MDes. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 503.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Industrial Design V: Thesis Ideation
courses.description: Ideation and prototyping phase of the thesis design project. This is the second course in the ID master's thesis project sequence for the MFA and MDes. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 504.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Industrial Design VI: Thesis Project Implementation
courses.description: Final studio course of the thesis design project, culminating in presentation of thesis project work in a public exhibition. This is the final course in the ID master's thesis project sequence for the MFA and MDes. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 505.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Membership in a DRI Research Team Project
courses.description: Design research is fundamentally interdisciplinary, often involving domain and process experts from a variety of fields. Students will choose to join one among several continuing peer- or faculty-led design research projects at various stages of completion. They will learn how to adapt their existing expertise to contribute productively to the project in its current stage, absorb insight from work completed at earlier stages, and collaborate with team members to advance the project toward its defined goals. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to students enrolled in the MFA or PhD program in Design for Responsible Innovation or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Leadership in a DRI Research Team Project
courses.description: Design research is fundamentally interdisciplinary, often involving domain and process experts from a variety of fields. Students will gain hands-on experience with design research team leadership by learning how to define, staff, and manage a new collaborative research project or new stage of a continuing project. Special attention will be paid to the distinctive features of the design research process such as the extended period of ambiguity and methods for eliciting significant contributions from team members with varied domain and process expertise. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 510. Enrollment in the MFA or PhD program in Design for Responsible Innovation or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Methods and Methodologies of Design
courses.description: Explores advanced pluriversal frameworks and systematic processes for tackling complex design challenges. Students will examine the theoretical foundations of design methodologies and relevant background literature while exploring specific methods for user research, problem framing, rapid prototyping, and evaluative testing. The course emphasizes the strategic integration of human-centered, more-than-human-centered, ethnographic, and collaborative tools to foster innovation in professional and academic design practice.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in an art and design degree program.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Ethical Integration of Technology in Design Practices
courses.description: Examine the complicated intersection of emerging technologies and responsible design practices. Critically evaluate the social, environmental, and cognitive impacts of integrating technologies such as AI, biotechnology, and automation within the design landscape. The course challenges students to critically analyze the benefits and costs of emerging technologies in the context of diverse design practices, and to move beyond a mindset of functional efficiency toward a framework of systemic accountability, equity, and long-term human and planetary well-being.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 513. Restricted to students with graduate standing in an art or design degree program.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Advanced Product Innovation
courses.description: Examines higher-level product design concepts, moving beyond form-making to emphasize strategic product ecosystems and innovations that disrupt conventional practices. The course is designed to prompt students to investigate how emerging technologies, user-driven research, and sustainable business models address complex, real-world challenges and IP concerns. Students will analyze these challenges across diverse settings, from technologically sophisticated urban centers to resource-limited environments. Students will explore solutions that are culturally meaningful and functionally robust, independent of technological resources.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to students with graduate standing in a design degree program.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Design for Responsible Innovation Research Impact
courses.description: This seminar helps DRI graduate students connect their research with pedagogy and professional development strategies to disseminate their research into publishing, conferences, communities, and other relevant venues. Students may take this course one time for credit toward the MFA DRI degree. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 8 hours.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Design for Responsible Innovation Research Methodology
courses.description: This seminar coordinates readings in design theory and the processes and principles of human-centered design with graduate students' emerging thesis research interests. Students will address the role of design research methodology in establishing design practice and design pedagogy. DRI graduate students enrolled in this course will be well-prepared to take leadership roles in the corresponding ARTD 270 Design Methods. Students may take this course one time for credit toward the MFA DRI degree. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 8 hours.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Fabrication and Manufacture
courses.description: Examines the essential relationship between design and production. Students will analyze various manufacturing methods, such as machining, casting, forming, and assembly, while building a precise vocabulary to communicate with makers and fabricators. Through hands-on experimentation with industrial materials, students will learn to refine designs for scalability, efficiency, and sustainability. The curriculum prioritizes “Design for Manufacturing” (DFM) principles, ensuring that innovative concepts are technically feasible and commercially viable.
courses.prereqText: ARTD 485 or Advanced Standing in MDes Industrial Design program.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Special Problems in Design
courses.description: Directed individual creative activity or research. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. Course Information: May be repeated if topics vary, in the same semester up to 10 hours; in separate semesters to a maximum of 20 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in Design.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: MFA Design for Responsible Innovation Studio
courses.description: This studio provides the MFA design student with tools to define and develop their body of work in the context of the DRI program's mission by pursuing an individual or collaborative path. The course enhances the student’s ability to develop a rigorous theoretical framework and select appropriate methods and processes for design research and pedagogy. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 20 hours.
courses.prereqText: Enrollment in the MFA concentration in Design for Responsible Innovation or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARTD
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: Faculty guidance in writing and depositing a thesis for MFA concentrations in Industrial Design or Design for Responsible Innovation or MDes Industrial Design. Students should enroll with the faculty member who is supervising their thesis. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in separate semesters to a maximum of 32 hours.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate study in Design For Responsible Innovation (MFA) or Industrial Design (MFA, MDes).
